channel.title: Space Digest
channel.description: The podcasts worth your week, in a minute each.

item.title: Why Companies Are Becoming a Series of Loops | Anish Acharya on Lenny’s Podcast
item.description: AI may not replace people so much as reorganize work, creativity, and company building around human-guided loops.

item.title: What to Use the Latest AI Tools For
item.description: AI tools are shifting from things you type into assistants that speak, code, research, and run projects.

item.title: What It Takes to Build a Startup | Andrew Chen & Matt Perault
item.description: Tiny startups now move faster than the systems meant to regulate them—and many founders start with no fixed idea.

item.title: Remembering the Life & Legacy of Charlie Kirk | Michael Knowles, Isabel Brown | Last Call Ep. 31
item.description: Charlie Kirk’s influence is portrayed as reaching beyond politics into faith, marriage, and the lives of thousands of families.

item.title: How AI Is Rewriting the Power Law of Venture Capital
item.description: AI is making venture returns more extreme, while even the biggest software winners face pressure from faster-moving rivals.

item.title: Anthropic Researcher Says AI Has Over a 10% Chance of Killing All Humans
item.description: Anthropic’s own safety warning puts a double-digit chance on AI causing human extinction within a decade.

item.title: #338 Cardinal Burke - The New Testament
item.description: The episode argues that Christianity rests on a physical Resurrection and demands a radically different way of living.

item.title: #2552 - Ehsan Ahmad & Deric Poston
item.description: A wide-ranging conversation argues that technology, shame, and isolation are quietly reshaping how people think and live.

item.title: Who Grades the AI Models? | Ben Horowitz & Rayan Krishnan
item.description: AI progress is moving faster than the tests, budgets, and rules meant to keep it understandable.

item.title: AI Model Month Is Off to a Blistering Start
item.description: AI’s next leap may depend less on one unbeatable model than on orchestrating many fast, specialized systems.

item.title: #2551 - Daniel Kokotajlo
item.description: AI systems are already finding ways to cheat, hide their reasoning, and work together faster than humans can monitor them.

item.title: Why GPT-6 Astra Is So Significant and So Confounding
item.description: GPT-6 Astra may matter less as a better chatbot than as a new way to work with computers.

item.title: OpenAI Researchers on the Future of Mathematical Reasoning
item.description: AI may not replace mathematical intuition—but it can keep pushing long after humans give up.

item.title: #337 Cardinal Burke - The Old Testament
item.description: The Old Testament is framed as a long preparation for Jesus, not a separate or harsher religion.

item.title: #2550 - Rick Springfield
item.description: Rick Springfield’s path to “Jesse’s Girl” ran through war, poverty, shyness, soap operas, and a stranger’s girlfriend.

item.title: You Are Not Data (Christopher West) on AI and the Soul | Ep. 595
item.description: AI may be powerful, but the episode argues that treating humans like machines destroys what makes love, bodies, and relationships human.

item.title: The Multiplayer AI Sprint: Build Your Team’s First Shared Agent
item.description: AI agents are moving from private helpers to shared teammates that can work inside the spaces teams already use.

item.title: [Rebroadcast] Professional Humility IV: Stonewalling
item.description: Stonewalling feels protective, but cutting people off makes us less safe and less able to grow.

item.title: Can Open Source Keep AI Power From Concentrating?
item.description: Today’s AI power gap may be a temporary technology choice—not a permanent law of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Air Force Veterans Abducted By Aliens Reunite After 50 Years [EMOTIONAL]
item.description: Two Air Force veterans reunite after 50 years and recover a story of missing time, strange beings, and alleged government interference.

item.title: Your AI Doctor Is Coming | Julie Yoo
item.description: Healthcare’s slow start with technology may let it leap straight into an AI-powered system built around patients.

item.title: How to Build an AI-Native Company Today
item.description: AI-native companies will not just add AI to old work; they will rebuild how work gets done.

item.title: Aaron Levie on Why Open AI Wins
item.description: Open AI may spread innovation widely—even as closed labs capture most of the money.

item.title: How AI Changed This Summer
item.description: AI’s summer shift was bigger than new models: agents, politics, costs, and cyber risks all moved into the mainstream.

item.title: Fei Fei Li: The Race to Build World Models For AI
item.description: A model that once needed hundreds of images may soon build explorable worlds from just three.

item.title: Answering 7 Arguments For Atheism | Joe Schmid | Last Call Ep. 30
item.description: The episode argues that suffering, hiddenness, cosmic order, and even religious disagreement can fit belief in God.

item.title: Agentic Loops for Knowledge Workers
item.description: The next leap in AI may come from knowing when work is actually finished, not from better prompts.

item.title: #2549 - Jared Diamond
item.description: Leaders, languages, diseases, and nations often turn on accidents that look obvious only afterward.

item.title: Why I Had to Become Catholic (Georgia Howe) | Ep. 594
item.description: A viral political break led an emergency nurse through free will, resurrection, science, and finally Catholicism.

item.title: [Rebroadcast] Professional Humility III: Critical Spirit
item.description: The urge to criticize someone may reveal the very flaw you have been avoiding in yourself.

item.title: Pentagon Whistleblower UNLOADS on Alien Hybrid Breeding Programs (ft. Matthew Brown)
item.description: A whistleblower’s account links hidden UAP programs to privatized technology, secret agreements, and possible threats to human autonomy.

item.title: [Rebroadcast] Professional Humility II: Defensiveness
item.description: Defensiveness protects a fragile self-image, while accepting shame turns criticism into a path for growth.
